passage:
At eleven at night, in his room in their Chandigarh flat, Baljeet was still going over the canteen scene. Kiran had been sitting with the debate team. Someone had said something and she had smiled at Manav. Just smiled. He'd replayed it maybe thirty times.
Then he opened her profile. A tagged photo from the debate trip: Kiran, Manav and four others at a dhaba. Manav's arm on the back of her chair. Or near it. Hard to tell.
He zoomed in. He checked who had liked it. He checked Manav's profile. Every detail looked like proof of something.
He messaged her: "u up?" She replied: "yes, studying, why?" He wrote, "nothing. just. do u like Manav?" She sent: "??? he's on my team. go to sleep baljeet 😅"
It should have helped. It didn't. He lay awake wondering what the three question marks really meant.

qa.q: Where was the tagged photo taken?
qa.a: The tagged photo was from the debate trip, at a dhaba.

qa.q: Why didn't Kiran's reply calm Baljeet?
qa.a: Baljeet was reading every detail as proof, so even a reassuring reply became something to worry over, like the three question marks.

qa.q: What could break Baljeet's loop tonight?
qa.a: Baljeet could put the phone away, notice that zooming and checking only feed the fear, and talk to a friend or family member instead of searching for proof.

qa.q: How might Kiran feel about the late-night question?
qa.a: Kiran seems puzzled and a bit amused, since Manav is just a teammate, and may not realise how anxious Baljeet has become.

grounding: Shows a teenage boy replaying a scene and scrolling his girlfriend's tagged photos, reading every ambiguous detail as proof, with reassurance feeding the fear.

passage:
"You've been on Sanjana's profile for an hour," Shankar said from the other bed.
"I'm just looking."
"At what?"
"This photo from the school trip. See how she's standing next to Vikram?"
"She's standing next to fifteen people."
"But she's smiling more in this one. And she didn't post anything with me last week."
"Because you were at your nani's."
Madhav scrolled. "And look, he liked her photo at 11:52. Who likes photos at 11:52?"
"Literally everyone, yaar."
"Maybe I should just ask her if she's hiding something."
"Madhav. Every time you look for proof that she's fine, you find a new thing to worry about. You've been doing this since Saturday."
Madhav put the phone face down on his chest. "I know. It's like I can't stop."
"Then stop for tonight. Put it on my side."

qa.q: What time did Vikram like the photo?
qa.a: Vikram liked her photo at 11:52.

qa.q: What does Madhav mean by 'It's like I can't stop'?
qa.a: Madhav feels stuck in a loop: each look for reassurance turns up a new worry, and the fear keeps growing.

qa.q: How did Shankar help Madhav in a useful way?
qa.a: Shankar pointed out that searching for proof feeds the worry and offered a simple step: put the phone away for the night.

qa.q: How might Sanjana feel if Madhav asks whether she's hiding something?
qa.a: Sanjana would likely feel hurt and accused over ordinary photos and likes, which could strain the relationship.

grounding: Illustrates a teen boy's rumination over his girlfriend's photos, where every detail seems like proof and seeking reassurance feeds the fear.

passage:
Seema didi,

You said write it down if it's eating me. So here.

On Friday I saw Jasnoor sitting with Arsh in the library. She was smiling. Since then I've replayed it maybe a hundred times. Was she leaning towards him? Was the smile the special one?

Then I went through her tagged photos. There's one from the school trip where Arsh is standing next to her. I zoomed in. His arm is behind her. Or maybe just behind the bench. I can't tell, which is worse.

I asked her on Saturday, "Is everything okay with us?" She said yes. I felt better for ten minutes. Then I thought, why did she take two seconds to answer?

Every time I check, I feel worse. But I can't stop checking.

Is this normal? Please don't laugh.

Your little brother,
Gurpreet

qa.q: Where did Gurpreet see Jasnoor sitting with Arsh?
qa.a: In the library.

qa.q: Why does Gurpreet feel worse every time he checks?
qa.a: He is anxious and afraid, and each ambiguous detail he finds, like the arm behind the bench, feeds the fear instead of easing it.

qa.q: What could help Gurpreet break the loop?
qa.a: Stop scrolling her photos, notice that asking for reassurance isn't working, and talk it through with Seema didi or another trusted person.

qa.q: How might Jasnoor feel being asked "Is everything okay with us?"
qa.a: She may be puzzled or a little uneasy, not knowing what brought it on, since she had just been in the library.

grounding: Gurpreet replays a scene, scrolls his girlfriend's tagged photos and reads every detail as proof, finding that seeking reassurance feeds his fear.

passage:
You want to know how bad it got? I'm Harman, and I'll tell you, because maybe someone needs to hear it.

Jasleen went to her cousin's birthday. Nandini was there, and a bunch of boys from her cousin's school. Jasleen posted one group photo. That's all.

I looked at that photo maybe fifty times. Who's the guy in the blue shirt? Why is he standing so close? Why did she only post one photo? What's she hiding in the others?

At 1 a.m. I texted her: "Did you have fun?" She said, "Yeah! Tired now, goodnight." And I lay there thinking, why so short? Who is she talking to instead?

The worst part is, I asked Nandini the next day, and she said nothing happened. I felt better for an hour. Then I started wondering if Nandini was covering for her.

Nothing anyone said could fix it. Because the fear wasn't coming from them.

qa.q: How many times did Harman look at the group photo?
qa.a: Maybe fifty times.

qa.q: What was Harman feeling at 1 a.m. after the short reply?
qa.a: Harman felt anxious and suspicious, reading the short reply as proof that Jasleen was talking to someone else.

qa.q: What does Harman's last line suggest could actually help?
qa.a: Since the fear comes from inside, looking at that fear, perhaps with a trusted adult, would help more than seeking more reassurance.

qa.q: How might Nandini feel if she learned Harman suspected her of covering?
qa.a: She would probably feel annoyed and insulted, having told the truth.

grounding: Harman replays a party photo, imagines the worst and reads every detail as proof, finding reassurance only feeds his fear.

passage:
Tuesday. At the bus stop Madhav saw Sanya share her earphones with Kunal from their class. They were laughing at something on her phone. Madhav got on the bus and said nothing. He replayed it all the way home.

Wednesday. He scrolled through Sanya's tagged photos until midnight. Kunal was in four of them. In one, from the dance practice, Kunal's hand was on her shoulder. Everyone's hands were on everyone's shoulders; it was a group dance. Madhav saw only Kunal's.

Friday, three days after the bus stop. He asked Sanya, "Do you like Kunal?" She laughed. "What? No! He's just funny." Madhav felt relieved. For one evening.

Saturday. He asked again, in a different way. "Why do you always sit near him?" Sanya's smile faded. "I don't. Why are you asking me this again?"

That night Madhav realised the answers weren't helping. The fear just waited, and came back.

qa.q: What did Sanya share with Kunal at the bus stop?
qa.a: Her earphones.

qa.q: How can you tell Madhav feels afraid again after each answer?
qa.a: He feels relieved for one evening after Sanya's answer, then anxious again the next day, asking in a different way.

qa.q: What turning point is open to Madhav at this stage?
qa.a: Noticing that asking again doesn't help, and turning to look at his own fear, perhaps with a trusted adult, instead of seeking more reassurance.

qa.q: What is it like for Sanya to be asked again on Saturday?
qa.a: She feels confused and a bit hurt, her smile fading, as the repeated questions start to feel like distrust.

grounding: Over several days Madhav replays a scene and scrolls Sanya's tagged photos, reading ambiguous details as proof, and finds each reassurance only feeds the fear.

passage: You think your Ujjwal Mama was always this calm? Listen, Seema. At sixteen I had a girlfriend, Kavita, and one evening I saw her at the bus stop sharing earphones with a boy from her tuition. That was all. But I went home and replayed it like a film. The angle of her head. Was she leaning? At night I scrolled through every photo she was tagged in, zooming in on hands and shoulders, reading old comments like a detective. A birthday party picture became proof. A late reply became proof. I even texted her friends, "Is she okay? She seems different," hoping they'd calm me. They did, for ten minutes, and then the fear came back hungrier. I was not looking for the truth, beta. I was feeding something that only ate evidence, and it was never full.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal see at the bus stop?
qa.a: He saw Kavita sharing earphones with a boy from her tuition.

qa.q: How did the young Ujjwal feel as he zoomed in on Kavita's tagged photos at night?
qa.a: He felt anxious and suspicious, replaying the scene and treating every photo and late reply as proof of what he feared.

qa.q: When the reassurance from Kavita's friends wore off after ten minutes, what could the young Ujjwal have done instead?
qa.a: He could have stopped scrolling, noticed that checking only fed his fear, and talked honestly with Kavita or a trusted adult about feeling insecure.

qa.q: What might Kavita have been experiencing while this went on?
qa.a: Kavita may have been unaware at first, then puzzled or uneasy when her friends were asked whether she seemed different.

grounding: Shows a jealous teenager replaying a scene and scrolling tagged photos, reading ordinary details as proof so that reassurance only feeds the fear.
